## Assessment

CHANGE NEEDED

One 3-line construct in `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`; `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` unchanged. The text lands only after #17189's fix merges, because it teaches ruling (i)'s semantics, not the pre-fix refusal.

Ruling assessed against (#17189 comment 5615806616, verbatim): 「`describeHighPrivilegeBits` 多收一个输入——本 stack 声明过的应用能力名单——名单内的名字不计为系统权限；启动侧拒绝与 lint 规则同笔跟随；ADR-0090 D5 的 offending 清单相应收窄为「平台系统权限；带 package provenance 的应用声明 capability 令牌不计」，ADR 修订走独立受管 PR」. Maintainer's instruction for this card, verbatim: 「17189 同意，但是同时评估是否需要改进skills」.

### Control

Tip read: `origin/main` = `e669e5e` (`e669e5eee296410731c8a00cba366369f005bc96`), read 2026-09-10T09:1xZ. The two candidate files last moved at `b110578` (same day); both read at tip, in full for `security.md` (210 lines) and by section for the platform file.

`git grep -n -iE 'isDefault|systemPermissions|capabilit|everyone|permission set' origin/main -- 'skills/**'` → **83 hits in 19 files**: `objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` 23 · `objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` 14 · `objectstack-data/SKILL.md` 10 · `objectstack-data/rules/security.md` 9 · `objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` 4 · `objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` 3 · `objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` 3 · `objectstack-data/references/_index.md` 3 · `objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` 2 · `objectstack-platform/references/_index.md` 2 · `objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` 2 · one each in `objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md`, `objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`, `objectstack-ui/references/_index.md`, `objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`, `objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`, `objectstack-data/rules/indexing.md`, `objectstack-data/evals/README.md`, `skills/README.md`.

- `isDefault`: exactly one hit, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md:122` (a list-view example).
- `everyone`: `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:78-79` (sharing-model table) and `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md:409` only.
- `systemPermissions` / `system_permissions`: **zero**. `defineCapability` / `scope: 'org'`: **zero** (second grep, exit 1).
- `capabilities` in `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`: the top-level key list at :76 (name only) and the `requires:` section :435-482, which teaches the 28 `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` (`kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`) — a different registry from the `capabilities:` stack key (`security/capabilities.ts`, ADR-0066 D1).

Positive control `git grep -c definePermissionSet origin/main -- 'skills/**'` → `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md:1`, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md:4` — identical to the PM's reading at `e669e5e`.

Zone-2 assumptions: **A holds** (as above). **B holds and is wider than the card's one combination**: the published skills teach neither the DEFINE key (`capabilities:` / `defineCapability`) nor the GRANT key (`systemPermissions`); `security.md:145`'s own `requiredPermissions: ['view_pii']` names an app token that no skill shows declared or granted anywhere (`view_pii` is not among the 9 curated `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES`). **C is falsified in one half** — see Reader.

### Reader

The reader is an AI author writing a metadata app's `permissions` (and `capabilities`) into the post-(i) world. Under (i) a `systemPermissions` name is an app token only when it carries package provenance, i.e. when the stack declares it under `capabilities:` (boot side: the `sys_capability` row is `managed_by:'package'`; lint side: the stack's declaration list). The back-compat implicit derivation that ADR-0066 D1 keeps alive seeds an *undeclared* name as `managed_by:'platform'` with no package provenance (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts` :9-11, :230). So after the fix:

- a **declared** app token on the `isDefault: true` set binds to `everyone` with no warning — hotclm's intended shape works;
- an **undeclared** app token on that set still reads as `'system permissions'`: `security-anchor-high-privilege` (error) and the boot refusal are unchanged, and the lint's fix-it hint (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` :781-783, "Split the powerful bits into a separate set granted through ordinary positions") walks the author into exactly hotclm#11's seven-per-position workaround instead of the declaration;
- a platform capability (`manage_users`, `setup.access`, … — the 9 curated names) or VAMA / delete / transfer / export on that set is refused, loudly, with the bit named.

Value gate:

① **Which decision the text changes:** whether to *declare* the token under `capabilities:` before granting it via `systemPermissions` on the `isDefault: true` set. Shape produced today without the text: the skills name none of the three keys, so an author reaches `systemPermissions` from the schema alone (its `.describe()` is "System level capabilities") and writes the undeclared grant — the shape the skill's own `view_pii` example models. **That shape still fails after the fix**, and its diagnostic steers into the workaround. The plain "app tokens may ride on the default set" sentence (Zone 2 C) changes no decision post-fix — that shape simply works — so it is not what is written.

② **Deletion or rewrite instead of addition:** no. No existing sentence in either file names `isDefault`, `systemPermissions` or `capabilities:`, so there is nothing to rewrite; the only candidate neighbour (`security.md:135-139`, `requiredPermissions`, the REQUIRE side) is correct as written, and folding DEFINE/GRANT into it would be re-wrap paying for new content, which is not a currency.

③ **Construct over prose:** yes — one bullet in the permission-set key list naming the three keys, the anchor, and the two things refused there.

Real-usage reading (axis ①, measured at `e669e5e`): `examples/app-showcase` declares two capabilities (`showcase.export_data`, `showcase.restricted_ops`, `src/security/capabilities.ts` :52, :77) and grants one on `OpsPermissionSet` (`permission-sets.ts` :220); its `isDefault` set `showcase_member_default` (:295-346) deliberately carries no `systemPermissions`. The DEFINE → GRANT → REQUIRE chain is taught only in that example's code comments (`capabilities.ts` :15-20), in no published skill. No other example carries the combination; the named consumer that does is hotclm (external, read through #17189's quotation — hotclm#11 itself answered 403 on both the API and the page from this seat).

Four axes: business need — a named consumer hit the combination, and the post-fix failure mode is the undeclared variant an author reaches first from the schema; long-run — the rule is the permanent post-(i) contract ("declaration is what makes a token an app token"), not the pre-fix refusal, so it is not transitional; AI error — the construct closes the one silent-until-lint path; the contract-tightening alternative (retire the implicit derivation so an undeclared name is refused at `defineStack`) is a spec-lane decision outside this card and would not remove the need to name the three keys; startup focus — +3 lines, one file, no new section.

### Proposal

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`** — insert one bullet after line 33, inside the existing key list of "## Object-level permissions (RBAC)". Neighbours, verbatim at `e669e5e`:

```
31: - Bits: `allowCreate` / `allowRead` / `allowEdit` / `allowDelete`, plus
32:   `allowTransfer` (ownership change), `viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords`
33:   (super-user, bypass sharing).
34: - Source: `node_modules/@objectstack/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`
```

Proposed bullet (becomes lines 34-36; widths 81 / 82 / 90 — the file's longest existing lines are 93):

```
- **`isDefault: true` = the `everyone` baseline (ADR-0090 D5).** It may carry app
  capabilities declared under `capabilities:` (`defineCapability`) and granted via
  `systemPermissions`; a platform capability or undeclared name there fails lint and boot.
```

Net: **+3 lines** in `security.md`. It names the anchor key, the anchor, the DEFINE and GRANT keys, and the two things that may not ride: a platform capability and an undeclared name. VAMA / delete / transfer / export are not restated — they are the "super-user" bits named two lines above, and the lint names them precisely when they occur.

**`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`** — **no change (0 lines)**. Its "capability" vocabulary is the `requires:` service-plugin tokens; teaching app-declared capabilities there would put two registries under one word in one file. `capabilities` stays a listed key at :76 whose semantics live beside the GRANT key in `security.md`.

Total net across both files: **+3** — within budget.

**Negative example (hotclm#11's seven per-position bindings): not included.** It is a pre-fix workaround, so text describing it is transitional (不渐进); an author following the construct never reaches it; it costs lines the budget does not have; and the one thing that steers a post-fix author toward it is the lint hint for the undeclared-name case, which lives in #17189's declared file surface (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture*`), not in a skill.

Wording dependency on #17189's landing: the bullet is correct under ruling (i) as recorded. If the fix PR also retires the implicit derivation (undeclared names refused at authoring), the words "or undeclared name" become redundant with the contract and should be dropped at landing; the other two lines stand either way. Two pre-fix sentences outside `skills/**` that the fix PR should move in the same diff are listed in the dev report below (`content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` :223-225, `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` :290-291).

### Blocked-by

Blocked-by: #17189
